concepts.why: The patient presents with pleuritic chest pain, muffled heart sounds, and a large pericardial effusion, which are all indicative of pericarditis.
The patient has a mediastinal mass accompanied by moderate pleural and pericardial effusions, which suggests the presence of an anterior mediastinal mass.
The patient presents with a 1-week history of dyspnea, intermittent fever, and decreased breath sounds at the right lower zone, which are all indicative of pneumonia.
The patient has muffled heart sounds and a heart rate of 120 beats/min, which may indicate myocarditis.
The patient has a history of intermittent fever and hepatomegaly, which may suggest tuberculosis.
The patient has a mediastinal mass and a large pericardial effusion, which may indicate lymphoma.
The patient has a history of intermittent fever and hepatomegaly, which may suggest sarcoidosis.
The patient has a mediastinal mass and a large pericardial effusion, which may indicate histiocytosis.
